about: Research sheet for the Vermont county edition. Every contact below was read on the date in reviewed_on from the page named beside it; scripts/make_county_state.py turns it into the edition files.
name: Vermont
phones_sentence: Veterans office phones and hours come from the Office of Veterans Affairs’ contact page. Its Veteran Service Officers work from Montpelier and serve every county.

offices.source_title: Vermont Office of Veterans Affairs: Contact Information for Organizations that Help Veterans and Their Families
offices.note: Veteran Service Officers help with VA claims, pension, survivor benefits and state veterans benefits at no charge. Certified service officers from the American Legion (802-296-5166), VFW (802-296-5168) and DAV (802-296-5167) also help any veteran apply; membership is not required.
offices.selection: Office address, phones and hours as printed on the Office of Veterans Affairs contact page, with the three veterans organizations’ certified service officers it lists; staff names omitted. Vermont has no county veterans offices, so every county shows the Montpelier office.

aging.source_title: Vermont Department of Disabilities, Aging and Independent Living: Older Americans Act snapshot with Area Agency on Aging map
aging.source_scope: Each Area Agency on Aging’s service area, with town exceptions, and phone; read in full. The document is dated February 15, 2019, though its title refers to 2023 data. The Department for Children and Families’ Area Agencies on Aging page (https://dcf.vermont.gov/contacts/partners/aaa; read in full, undated) gives the same service areas and the statewide HelpLine, 1-800-642-5119.
aging.next_step_extra: The statewide Senior HelpLine, 1-800-642-5119, also reaches your local agency.

regions.label: Champlain Valley
regions.name: Age Well
notes: In Addison County, Granville and Hancock are served by Central Vermont Council on Aging (802-479-0531).

regions.label: Southwestern Vermont
regions.name: Southwestern Vermont Council on Aging
notes: Pittsfield (Rutland County) is served by Central Vermont Council on Aging (802-479-0531); Readsboro, Searsburg and Winhall (Bennington County) by Senior Solutions (802-885-2655).

regions.label: Central Vermont
regions.name: Central Vermont Council on Aging
notes: In Orange County, Thetford is served by Senior Solutions (802-885-2655).
This agency also serves Granville and Hancock (Addison County), Pittsfield (Rutland County), and Bethel, Rochester, Royalton, Sharon and Stockbridge (Windsor County).

regions.label: Southeastern Vermont
regions.name: Senior Solutions (Council on Aging for Southeastern Vermont)
notes: In Windsor County, Bethel, Rochester, Royalton, Sharon and Stockbridge are served by Central Vermont Council on Aging (802-479-0531).
This agency also serves Readsboro, Searsburg and Winhall (Bennington County) and Thetford (Orange County).

regions.name: Vermont Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program (Vermont Legal Aid)
regions.source_title: Vermont Legal Aid: Vermont Long-Term Care Ombudsman Project
regions.source_scope: Call 1-800-889-2047 ext. 3 or use the online form; replies within three business days; serves people in licensed long-term care facilities and people getting care at home through Choices for Care; read in full. The program is statewide, so every county shows it.
notes: Ask for extension 3, the ombudsman. Expect a reply within three business days.

list.name: Vermont Center for Independent Living
notes: Main office: 11 East State Street, Montpelier, VT 05602. Toll-free 800-639-1522; Relay 711.
Other offices: Burlington 802-861-2896; Morrisville 802-888-2180; Bennington 802-447-0574; Brattleboro 802-254-6851; Newport 802-334-9000 (call for an appointment); Rutland 802-779-9021.

programs.name: Vermont veterans: Office of Veterans Affairs for claims help
programs.description: Free help applying for VA benefits from the Office of Veterans Affairs’ Veteran Service Officers in Montpelier, who serve the whole state. Certified service officers from the American Legion, VFW and DAV also help any veteran apply; membership is not required.
programs.next_step: Call 802-828-3379 or, within Vermont, 888-666-9844 (weekdays 7:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.). Or call a service officer: American Legion 802-296-5166, VFW 802-296-5168, DAV 802-296-5167.
constraints: Call before visiting; the office serves the whole state from Montpelier.

sources.title: Vermont Office of Veterans Affairs: Contact Information for Organizations that Help Veterans and Their Families
sources.scope: Office address, main and toll-free lines, hours, and the certified Veteran Service Officers of the American Legion, VFW and DAV; read in full.

programs.name: Vermont Area Agencies on Aging and the Senior HelpLine
programs.organization: Vermont’s five Area Agencies on Aging
programs.description: Vermont’s five Area Agencies on Aging give information and help to people 60 and older and their families: help at home, meals, caregiver support, health insurance counseling and more. One statewide HelpLine reaches all five. Military service is not required.
programs.next_step: Call the Senior HelpLine at 1-800-642-5119, or choose a county above for its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

sources.title: Vermont Department for Children and Families: Area Agencies on Aging
sources.scope: The five agencies’ service areas and the statewide line, 1-800-642-5119; read in full.

sources.title: Vermont Department of Disabilities, Aging and Independent Living: Older Americans Act snapshot with Area Agency on Aging map
sources.scope: Each agency’s phone and service area; read in full. Dated February 15, 2019.

programs.name: Medicare counseling (Vermont SHIP)
programs.organization: Vermont State Health Insurance Assistance Program, through the Area Agencies on Aging
programs.description: Free, confidential Medicare counseling from certified counselors at Vermont’s five Area Agencies on Aging: plan choices, Part D, Medigap and help paying for Medicare. The Senior HelpLine connects you to a counselor near you.
programs.next_step: Call the Senior HelpLine at 1-800-642-5119 and ask for a SHIP counselor. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Counseling is by appointment. Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.
programs.phone_label: Vermont SHIP through the Senior HelpLine (800-642-5119)

programs.name: Vermont Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
programs.organization: Vermont Legal Aid, Long-Term Care Ombudsman Project; Department of Disabilities, Aging and Independent Living, Adult Protective Services
programs.description: Advocacy for people in licensed long-term care facilities and people getting care at home through Choices for Care. Adult Protective Services takes reports of abuse, neglect or exploitation of vulnerable adults.
programs.next_step: Call the ombudsman at 1-800-889-2047, extension 3, or use the online form. To report abuse, call your local or state police and Adult Protective Services at 1-800-564-1612. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

sources.title: Vermont Legal Aid: Vermont Long-Term Care Ombudsman Project
sources.scope: Phone and extension, online form, response time and who the program serves; read in full.

sources.title: Vermont Attorney General: Elder Protection Initiative
sources.scope: Report abuse, neglect or exploitation to local or state police and to Adult Protective Services at 1-800-564-1612; search excerpt.

programs.name: Free legal help for older Vermonters
programs.organization: Vermont Legal Aid, Elder Law Project; Legal Services Vermont
programs.description: Vermont Legal Aid’s Elder Law Project gives free civil legal help to Vermonters 60 and older: abuse and financial exploitation, housing and benefits, and individual rights and advance planning. Legal Services Vermont runs the statewide helpline.
programs.next_step: Call the statewide legal helpline at 1-800-889-2047, or ask for help online at vtlawhelp.org.
constraints: Offices have limited in-person hours; call or use the online form first.

sources.title: Vermont Legal Aid: Elder Law Project brochure
sources.scope: Full range of civil legal services to Vermonters 60 and over, including abuse and financial exploitation, housing and benefits, and advance planning; helpline 1-800-889-2047; search excerpt.

sources.title: Vermont Law Help: Locations and Contact Information
sources.scope: Statewide helpline 1-800-889-2047; limited in-person office hours; search excerpt.

programs.name: VA health care in Vermont
programs.organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, VA White River Junction Healthcare System
programs.description: Vermont veterans are served by the VA White River Junction Healthcare System: the White River Junction VA Medical Center (163 Veterans Drive, White River Junction; 802-295-9363, toll-free 866-687-8387) and its outpatient clinics.
programs.next_step: Call 802-295-9363 or 866-687-8387 for appointments or the 24-hour nurse line. Not enrolled yet? Ask a Veteran Service Officer for help applying.
constraints: If a service you need is not offered near you, ask about travel benefits and community care.
programs.phone_label: White River Junction VA Medical Center (802-295-9363)

sources.scope: 24-hour nurse, appointment changes and telephone care: 802-295-9363 or 866-687-8387; search excerpt.
